title: Surjectivity on stack points detects representable surjectivity
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$, let $\mathcal Y$ be either an algebraic stack over $S$ or an algebraic space over $S$ (regarded as the category fibred in sets of its sections, with the point classes of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]), and let $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ be a morphism representable by algebraic spaces. An algebraic stack over $S$ means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, representability and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and algebraic spaces are [def-trf-algebraic-space]. In particular representability of $f$ means that $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is an algebraic space for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$. Use the field-valued point classes of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Then $|f|:|\mathcal Y|\to|\mathcal X|$ is surjective if and only if, for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the projection $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}T\to T$ is surjective on underlying algebraic-space point sets. No flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ is required.

source.place: Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective), equivalence (1) <=> (2), with the scheme-base-change meaning of (2) spelled out in its proof. The case of an algebraic-space source uses that an algebraic space is an algebraic stack, algebraic.tex Tag 03YS (lemma-representable-algebraic), (2).

proof.text: Assume $|f|$ is surjective. Fix a scheme map $g:T\to\mathcal X$ and a point $t\in|T|$, represented by $t_0:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$. Representability gives the algebraic space $P=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}T$. Choose a field-valued representative $y:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal Y$ whose class maps to $[g t_0]$. By the definition of stack point classes in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open], there are a common extension field $M$ of $L$ and $\kappa(t)$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:f(y_M)\xrightarrow{\sim}g(t_{0,M})$. By the fibrewise triple definition of the 2-fibre product in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], $(y_M,t_{0,M},\alpha)$ is an object of $P$ over $\operatorname{Spec}M$. Its algebraic-space point class, in the convention of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], maps to $t$: the representative $t_{0,M}$ is the restriction of $t_0$ to $M$. Thus every $t$ has a preimage. This works for each $T$ and $g$.

source.place: Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective), forward implication, expanding Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian) by the defining common-field 2-isomorphism and the defining 2-fibre-product triple.

proof.text: Conversely assume every scheme base change is surjective on point sets. Represent any $x\in|\mathcal X|$ by $x_0:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$, using [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Apply the hypothesis to $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$. The unique point of $T$ has a preimage in $P=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}K$. Choose a representative $z:\operatorname{Spec}M\to P$ of that preimage, using [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. The second projection gives a field homomorphism $K\to M$, hence an extension field. The defining triple of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives an object $y_M$ of $\mathcal Y(M)$ and an isomorphism $f(y_M)\cong(x_0)_M$. Therefore $|f|([y_M])=[x_0]=x$. For an algebraic-space source the same argument applies to its discrete fibred groupoid: isomorphisms in its fibres are equalities, so its point classes are exactly those of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Both directions use representability only to make $P$ an algebraic space; neither uses flatness or finite presentation.
